title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 distribution artifacts contained credential-stealing malware
summary: LiteLLM confirms malicious PyPI wheels and container artifacts for 1.107.0. The malware steals credentials and loads remote code-execution tools; the official GitHub source tag did not contain the malicious files.

severity.rationale: A widely used agent dependency was distributed with credential-stealing code. Merely starting Python in the affected environment can rerun it, so package replacement alone is insufficient.

affected.note: Exactly 1.107.0: all seven wheels. Container variants and affected image tags are listed in the vendor incident report; this is an artifact compromise, not an affected-version interval.

exposure: Exposure depends on installing the malicious PyPI wheels or running affected images. Private enterprise registry releases were not impacted.

params.instructions: Check installation history for litellm 1.107.0 and compare container digests with the vendor incident report. Do not start Python or pip in a suspected environment.

remediation.details: Avoid starting Python or pip before containment. Follow the vendor cleanup guidance, stop the detached loader, rebuild affected environments with a verified clean release, and rotate reachable credentials from a trusted environment. The incident report recommends pinning 1.106.2.
remediation.risk: High. Rebuilding environments and rotating credentials can interrupt services.

verification: Verify malicious startup files and loader persistence are removed, the replacement artifacts are trusted, and credential rotation is complete.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
